To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose a PTAS for the problem of determining an optimal task-to-processor mapping for a given task system upon a two-type heterogeneous multiprocessor platform.

(i) we propose a PTAS for the problem of assigning implicit-deadline task sets on two-type heterogeneous multiprocessors; (ii) our PTAS offers an upper bound of 1+3ε on the speedup of processors, which is the best possible upper bound; (iii) our PTAS is the first to offer such an upper bound; and (iv) our PTAS out-performs the state-of-art PTAS in terms of the required processor speedup.
we have designed a PTAS that is faster than the state-of-the-arts, and that for the vast majority, it requires significantly fewer processors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of scheduling sporadic tasks upon multiprocessor platforms.

the problem of determining an assignment of sporadic tasks to a platform in which there is a heterogeneous set of processors, some of which are more powerful (and hence more costly to acquire) than others.
the problem of assigning implicit-deadline task sets on heterogeneous multiprocessors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our PTAS is the best known PTAS for this important problem.
our PTAS outperform all existing PTAS for the problem of assigning sporadic tasks on two-type heterogeneous multiprocessors.
our PTAS is the best PTAS for this problem to date.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide the first polynomial-time approximation guarantee for the problem under consideration, and our proposed PTAS is practically efficient and effective.
our PTAS is not only the first PTAS for this important problem, but it also outperforms the existing PTAS in both theory and practice.
we have proposed a PTAS for the problem of assigning sporadic tasks to a platform in which there is a single processor of a faster type and multiple processors of a slower type.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the problem of determining task-to-processor assignments upon heterogeneous multiprocessors can be solved efficiently, even when the number of processors is large.
, for the problem of scheduling implicit-deadline task sets upon a two-type heterogeneous platform, a PTAS is possible.
, for the problem at hand, a PTAS with a small processor speedup can be designed.
